summary: Defines IbisBackend, the package's single entry point for Ibis-supported databases, and IbisConnection, the live-connection wrapper. IbisBackend is constructed from a SettingsParameters object, a connection URL, or a dialect name plus driver kwargs; connect() composes an optional auth profile at connect time. It exposes inspection (list/inspect tables, namespaces, catalogs, indexes), fluent DDL/DML (create/drop table and view, insert, truncate, rename, upsert, add_columns, index ops), query helpers (table, run_sql, run_expr, to_sql), connection adoption (from_ibis_connection, from_raw_connection with optional session-option preservation), and explicit transaction scopes (transaction, in_transaction, native_transaction_open, raw_driver_connection). Operations dispatch to a per-dialect hook when one is registered, otherwise to the generic sqlglot-rendered implementation driven by the DialectSpec.
extension_points: New dialects are added as DialectSpec entries in dialects/_registry.py; IbisBackend dispatches through spec fields without per-dialect subclasses

Per-dialect hook fields on DialectSpec (upsert_hook, add_columns_hook, rename_table_hook, truncate_table_hook, create_index_hook, drop_index_hook, list_indexes_hook) override the generic implementations
from_ibis_connection / from_raw_connection let callers hand in their own live connection (owns_connection=False by default)
lifecycle_notes: connect() is idempotent and returns self; auth profile is applied at connect time, not construction
Context-manager use connects on __enter__ and closes on __exit__
close() raises RuntimeError inside an open transaction() scope on the same native handle; an adopted connection is released but not disconnected
After an ambiguous COMMIT failure on an owned connection the connection is discarded so it is not reused
Mutating operations return self for chaining; terminal operations return data
documentation_hooks: Three construction paths: SettingsParameters, URL string, dialect= keyword
Missing driver extras raise ImportError naming pip install 'mountainash-data[<dialect>]'
Namespace rendering: native ops accept catalog-qualified single-level namespaces; manual-SQL ops (upsert, add_columns, index ops) reject catalog qualification
transaction() ownership semantics on sqlite/duckdb/postgres: begin+own when idle, join without completing when a caller transaction is open
in_transaction() vs native_transaction_open(): package scope registration vs driver state
URL credentials are stripped from the URL and passed as a PasswordAuthProfile; errors never echo the URL
risks: IbisConnection.list_namespaces/list_tables/list_catalogs print the error to stdout and return [] outside a transaction scope, which can mask connection or permission failures
IbisConnection docstrings still refer to core.protocol.Connection, which no longer exists (only Backend is defined in core/protocol.py)
to_sql() does not run inside the _protected() wrapper (compile only, no database work), unlike the other operations
Transaction ownership semantics apply only to OWNERSHIP_DIALECTS (sqlite, duckdb, postgres); other transactional dialects keep plain BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK behaviour
from_raw_connection is gated on DialectSpec.raw_adoption_verified, currently True only for duckdb and motherduck
open_questions: Should the stdout print fallbacks in IbisConnection list_* methods become logging or warnings?

evidence.detail: IbisBackend re-exported at the package root
_import_ibis_backend translates ModuleNotFoundError into ImportError naming the mountainash-data[<dialect>] extra
from_raw_connection snapshots/restores adoption_mutations in a finally block when preserve_session=True
transaction() delegates to _transaction.run_transaction with spec probes and on_commit_failure=_discard_connection
Quick start and transaction semantics document IbisBackend usage
